lane: 1 عَوِرَ ذ , (O, K,) said of a man, (O,) aor. يَعْوَرُ , inf. n. عَوَرٌ , (S, O, K,) He was, or became, blind of one eye: (K:) [or he became one-eyed; wanting one eye: or one of his eyes sank in its socket: or one of his eyes dried up: see what next follows:] as also عَارَ , aor. يَعَارُ ; and ; (K;) and . (Sgh, K.) And عَوِرَتْ عَيْنُهُ , (Az, S, IKtt, O, Msb,) aor. تَعْوَرُ , (Az, Msb,) inf. n. عَوَرٌ ; (IKtt, Msb;) and عَارَتْ , aor. تَعَارُ (Az, S, IKtt, O) and تِعَارُ ; (IKtt, TA;) and ; (Az, S, IKtt, O;) and ; (Az, O, TA;) His eye became blind: (TA:) or became wanting: or sank in its socket: (Msb:) or dried up. (IKtt, TA.) Ibn-Ahmar says, أَعَارَتْ عَيْنُهُ أَمْ لَمْ تَعَارَا [ Has his eye become blind or has it not indeed become blind? ] meaning تَعَارَنْ ; but, pausing, he makes it to end with ا : in عَوِرَتْ , the و is preserved unaltered because it is so preserved in the original form, which is اِعْوَرَّتْ , on account of the quiescence of the letter immediately preceding: then the augmentatives, the ا and the teshdeed, are suppressed, and thus the verb becomes عَوِرَ : for that اعورّت is the original form is shown by the form of the sister-verbs, اِسْوَدَّ and اِحْمَرَّ ; and the analogy of verbs significant of faults and the like, اِعْرَجَّ and اِعْمَىَّ as the original forms of عَرِجَ and عَمِىَ ; though these may not have been heard. (S, O. [See also صَيِدَ .]) -b2- عَارَتِ الرَّكِيَّةُ , aor. تَعُورُ [or تَعْوَرُ or تَعَارُ ?], (tropical:) The well became filled up. (TA.) -A2- عَارَهُ , (O, K,) aor. يَعُورُهُ ; (TA;) and , (K,) inf. n. إِعْوَارٌ ; (TA;) and , (K,) inf. n. تَعْوِيرٌ ; (TA;) He rendered him blind of one eye. (K.) And عَارَ عَيْنَهُ , (S, M, IKtt, O, Msb,) aor. يَعُورُهَا , (S, O, Msb,) inf. n. عَوْرٌ : (IKtt;) and (more commonly, M) ; and ; (S, M, IKtt, Msb;) He put out his eye: (IKtt, Msb: *) or made it to sink in its socket. (Msb.) Some say that عُرْتُ عَيْنَهُ and [sic] are from عَائِرٌ , q. v. (TA.) -b2- عَارَ الرَّكِيَّةَ and signify the same as , (tropical:) He marred, or spoiled, the well, so that the water dried up: (A, TA:) or he filled it up with earth, so that the springs thereof became stopped up: and in like manner, عُيُونَ الميَاهِ he stopped up the sources of the waters: (Sh, TA:) and عَيْنَ الرَّكِيَّةِ he filled up the source of the well, so that the water dried up. (S.) -A3- عَارَهُ , aor. يَعُورُهُ and يَعِيرُهُ , (S, K,) or the aor. is not used, or, accord. to IJ, it is scarcely ever used, (TA,) or some say يُعُورُهُ , (Yaakoob,) or يَعِيرُهُ , (Aboo-Shibl,) He, or it, took, and went away with, him, or it: (S, O, K:) or destroyed him, or it. (K, TA.) One says, مَا أَدْرِى أَىُّ الجَرَادِ عَارَهُ I know not what man went away with him, or it: (S, O, TA:) or took him, or it. (TA.) It is said to be only used in negative phrases: but Lh mentions أَرَاكَ عُرْتَهُ , and عِرْتَهُ , I see thee, or hold thee, to have gone away with him, or it: [see also art. عير :] IJ says, It seems that they have scarcely ever used the aor. of this verb because it occurs in a prov. respecting a thing that has passed away. (TA.) -A4- See also 3 in art. عر .

headwords.def: (O, K,) said of a man, (O,) aor. يَعْوَرُ, inf. n. عَوَرٌ, (S, O, K,) He was, or became, blind of one eye: (K:) [or he became one-eyed; wanting one eye: or one of his eyes sank in its socket: or one of his eyes dried up: see what next follows:] as also عَارَ, aor. يَعَارُ; and; (K;) and. (Sgh, K.) And عَوِرَتْ عَيْنُهُ, (Az, S, IKtt, O, Msb,) aor. تَعْوَرُ, (Az, Msb,) inf. n. عَوَرٌ; (IKtt, Msb;) and عَارَتْ, aor.
عَوَّرَ see 1, in five places: and see 3.

عاورهُ الشَّىْءَ He did with the thing like as he (the other) did with it: (S:) [or he did the thing with him by turns; for] المُعَاوَرَةُ is similar to المُدَاوَلَةُ, with respect to a thing that is between two, or mutual. (TA. [See also 6.]) See also 4. عاور المَكَايِيلَ i. q. عَايَرَهَا; [q. v. in art. عير;] (S, O, K;) as also. (K.)

أَعْوَرَ see 1, in four places. اعارهُ الشَّىْءَ, (Az, Msb, K,) inf. n. إِعَارَةٌ and; like as you say أَطَاعَهُ, inf. n. إِطَاعَةٌ and طَاعَةٌ, and أَجَابَهُ, inf. n. إِجَابَةٌ and جَابَةٌ; (Az, Msb;) [or rather عَارَةٌ is a quasi-inf. n.; and so is طَاعَةٌ, and جَابَةٌ;] and اعارهُ مِنْهُ; and إِيَّاهُ; (K;) [accord. to the TK, all signify He lent him the thing: but the second seems rather to signify he lent him of it: and respecting the third, see 3 above.] For three exs., see 10.
تَعَوَّرَ see 6: see also 10, in two places: and see 5 in art. عير.

تعاوروا الشَّىْءِ , and, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) and, (S, O, K,) They took the thing, or did it, by turns; syn. تَدَاوَلُوهُ, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) فِيمَا بَيْنَهُمْ: (S, O, TA:) the و is apparent [not changed into ا ] in اعتوروا because it signifies the same as تعاوروا. (S.) Aboo-Kebeer says, وَإِ َا الكُمَاةُ تَعَاوَرُوا طَعْنَ الكُلَى [ And when the men clad in armour interchange the piercing of the kidneys ]. (TA.) And in a trad.
إِعْتَوَرَ see 6, in five places.
إِعْوَرَّ see 1, first quarter, in two places.

and (O, K) He asked, or demanded, or sought, what is termed عَارِيَّة [ a loan ]. (K.) It is said in the story of the [golden] calf, مِنْ حَلْىٍ بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ i. e. اِسْتَعَارُوهُ [ Of ornaments which the children of Israel had asked to be lent, or had borrowed ]. (TA.) You say also اِسْتَعَرْتُ مِنْهُ الشَّىْءَ, (Mgh, Msb, K, *) and اِسْتَعَرْتُهُ الشَّىْءَ, (Mgh, TA,) suppressing the preposition, (Mgh,) I asked of him the loan of the thing [ and he lent it to me ].
إِعْوَاْرَّ see 1, first quarter, in two places.

inf. n. of عَوِرَ [q. v.]. (S, O, K.) See also عَوَرَةٌ. Also Weakness, faultiness, or unsoundness; and so: badness, foulness, or unseemliness, in a thing: disgrace, or disfigurement. (TA.) [See also عَوَارٌ.] هٰ َا الأَمْرُ بَيْنَنَا عَوَرٌ means This is a thing, or an affair, that we do by turns. (TA, voce رَوَحٌ.)

(tropical:) A thing having no keeper or guardian; [lit., having a gap, or an opening, or a breach, exposing it to thieves and the like;] as also. (TA.) You say مَكَانٌ (tropical:) A place in which one fears: (TA:) a place in which ( فِيهِ [in one of my copies of the S مِنْهُ ]) one fears being cut [or pierced (see 4)]; (S, TA;) as also مَكَانٌ; which is doubly tropical: (TA:) and طَرِيقٌ (tropical:) a road in which is an opening, in which one fears losing his way and being cut off: and…
: see 4: and see also عَارِيَّةٌ.

The pudendum, or pudenda, (S, O, Msb, K,) of a human being, (S, O,) of a man and of a woman: (TA:) so called because it is abominable to uncover, and to look at, what is thus termed: (Msb:) said in the B to be from عَارٌ, meaning مَ َمَّةٌ: (TA:) [but see what is said voce عَارِيَّةٌ: the part, or parts, of the person, which it is indecent to expose: ] in a man, what is between the navel and the knee: and so in a woman: (Jel in xxiv.

a subst. meaning [q. v.]: (O:) [it is mentioned in the S as a subst., and app., from the context, as signifying عَوَرٌ, i. e. A blindness of one eye: (but expl. by Golius as meaning the succession of a worse after a better: ) after the mention of رَجُلٌ أَعْوَرُ, and the phrase بَدَلٌ أَعْوَرُ and خَلَفٌ أَعْوَرُ, in the S, it is added, وَالاِسْمُ العَوَرَةُ, or, accord. to one copy, العَوْرَةُ; and then follows, وَقَدْ عَارَتِ العَيْنُ.]
a pl. of أَعْوَرُ [q. v.]; as also عِيرَانٌ. It is also used as a sing.; رَكِيَّةٌ عُورَانٌ meaning (assumed tropical:) A well in a state of demolition. (O, K.)

(S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) and sometimes عَارِيَةٌ, without teshdeed, (Msb, K,) when used in poetry, (Msb,) and, (S, O, K,) What is taken by persons by turns; expl. by مَا تَدَاوَلُوهُ بَيْنَهُمْ: (K:) [generally meaning a loan: and the act of lending; ] the putting one in possession of the use of a thing without anything given in exchange: (KT, and Kull p.

(S, Mgh, Msb, K) and (AZ, S, Msb, K) and (K) A fault; a defect; an imperfection; a blemish; something amiss; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) in an article of merchandise, (S, Mgh, Msb,) and in a garment, or piece of cloth, (TA,) and in a slave, (Msb,) and in a beast: (TA:) or in a garment, or piece of cloth, a hole, and a rent; (Lth, Mgh, Msb, K, TA;) and so in the like, and in a house or tent and the like; (TA;) and in a garment, or piece of cloth, also a burn; and a rottenness: (Mgh:) and some…
: see عَوَارٌ, in two places.
: see أَعْوَرُ, of which it is the dim.
عَيِّرَةُ عَيْنَيْنِ : see عَائِرٌ.
: see عَائِرٌ, in four places.

Anything that causes disease in the eye, (K, TA,) and wounds: so called because the eye becomes closed on account of it, and the person cannot see, the eye being as it were blinded: (TA:) ophthalmia; syn. رَمَدٌ; (S, O, K;) as also: (Msb:) which latter also signifies foul, thick, white matter, that collects in the inner corner of the eye; not fluid; syn.

Blind of one eye: (K:) one-eyed; wanting one eye: or having one of his eyes sunk in its socket: (Msb:) or having one of his eyes dried up: (IKtt:) applied to a man, (S, Msb,) and to a camel, &c.: (TA:) fem. عَوْرَآءُ: (Msb:) pl. عُورٌ and عُورَانٌ (O, K) and عِيرَانٌ. (K.) The أَعْوَر is considered by the Arabs as of evil omen. (TA.) It is said in a prov., أَعْوَرُ عَيْنَكَ وَالحَجَرَ [ O oneeyed, preserve thine eye (thine only eye) from the stone ]. (Meyd, TA.) Squint-eyed; syn.
[inf. n. of 10. And hence, (tropical:) A metaphor ].
: see عَوِرٌ, in four places.

[ Borrowed; or asked, demanded, or sought, as a loan; ] pass. part. n. of 10 as used in the phrase اِسْتَعَارَهُ ثَوْبًا [q. v.] so in the following verse of Bishr (S, O) Ibn-Abee-Házim, describing a horse: (O:) كَأَنَّ حَفِيفَ مَنْخِرِهِ إِ َا مَا كَتَمْنَ الرَّبْوُ كِيرٌ مُسْتَعَارُ [ As though the sound of the wind of his nostril, when they (i. e.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
